blocks.text: An inventor discloses an invention to the IP Legal team using a standardized invention disclosure form. Legal has 30 days from receipt of the disclosure to assess patentability and notify the inventor of its determination.
If the invention is deemed patentable, Legal prepares a provisional patent application within 60 days of the original disclosure date.

The CTO must approve the provisional application before it is filed. Engineering must confirm that no third-party IP is incorporated into the invention prior to filing. CTO approval and Engineering IP confirmation may be obtained in parallel.

The provisional application must be filed before the 1-year statutory bar date. If the inventor has already published or publicly disclosed the invention, the filing must occur within 12 months of first publication.

messages.text: Heads up: as of Q1 2026 Legal requires inventors to complete a prior art search form and attach it to the disclosure before patentability assessment begins.
Can we file continuation patents in other countries simultaneously? Asking for a project.
What happens if the inventor leaves the company before the provisional is filed? Just a hypothetical.
Should we move to using continuation-in-part filings more aggressively? Heard competitors do it.
